title: Lender-Placed Flood Master Programs — Master Policy Conditions on Certificate Start Date, Term and Premium
content:
**Start date.** When a certificate may start on the lapse date (every tier allows it) and the first notice on the loan was mailed no later than 90 calendar days (the lapse-date reporting window) after the lapse date, the certificate starts on the lapse date, so the lender may charge the borrower from the date coverage lapsed or became insufficient; otherwise it starts on the date it is issued.

**Term.** A certificate of the **Lender-Placed Flood Master Programs** runs 12 calendar months from its start.

**Premium.** The annual premium is the building limit divided by 100 times the tier's building rate per 100 plus the contents limit divided by 100 times the tier's contents rate per 100, rounded to the cent, and never less than the tier's minimum certificate premium. **This sentence is no longer in force for the premiums priced under the residential placement schedule, the residential renewal schedule and the commercial placement schedule; every other certificate premium remains computed this way.**

**Billing.** The full annual premium is billed to the lender on the statement for the month the certificate is issued or renewed.

| First notice mailed, counted from the lapse date | Certificate start |
|---|---|
| On or before the 90th calendar day after the lapse date | The lapse date |
| Later than that | The date the certificate is issued |

## Points of judgement

- *Is the premium prorated when a certificate starts on the lapse date?* No: the full annual premium is billed on the statement for the month of issue.
